title: Worst to First: Sonny's Long Ride From the Cellar to the Buckaroo Bowl Throne
body: Every league needs a founding father, and the Buckaroo Football League's founder spent his first two seasons as its foundation, in the most literal, basement-level sense. Sonny launched Ben Dover in 2023 and went 6-8 with 1,413.3 points, sneaking in as the 5 seed before the consolation ladder delivered him to sixth place out of six. For a guy who built the league website, it was a bold choice to make his own team page the saddest one on it. He made 10 pickups and zero trades that year, which suggests he was at least trying. Mostly.

Then came 2024, which can only be described as a commissioner going into witness protection. Ben Dover went 5-9, scored 1,304.3 points, landed the 6 seed and finished last again, completing the league's first and only back-to-back cellar run. The transaction log tells the story: zero trades and exactly one pickup all season. The low point arrived in week 12, when Mekhi held him to a career-worst 44.1 points, a number that looks less like a fantasy score and more like a typo.

And then, out of nowhere, 2025 happened. Sonny woke up, attacked the waiver wire with 22 pickups, made his first trade ever, and turned Ben Dover into a 13-3 juggernaut that piled up 1,850.8 points and grabbed the 1 seed. His career-best 153.4 came in week 10 against Randy, a beatdown that still shows up in Randy's complaints. He won his only playoff game and lifted the Buckaroo Bowl III trophy, snapping Kaushal's two-title streak and pulling off the most complete worst-to-first arc this league has ever seen. Somewhere, a conspiracy theorist is still checking whether the commish quietly edited the scoring settings.

The rivalry ledger shows a guy who has beaten up most of the league. He's 7-5 against both Ramon and Mekhi, 6-5 against Alan, and 5-3 against Randy, who has given up more than his share of misery to the commissioner. The one veteran with his number is Kaushal, who leads the series 6-5, a fitting edge for the two-time champ whose dynasty Sonny ended. Among the 2026 newcomers he's 1-0 against Jordan, but rookie Zoe took their first meeting, which means Sonny has already been introduced to the cold hard reality of a Wisconsin winter.

Now he's rebranded as The Horse is Hea, and the horse is very much still running. Through seven weeks he's 5-2 with 853.6 points, has already made 2 trades and 17 pickups, and holds 28 percent title odds as he hunts back-to-back crowns in the league's first eight-team season. The guy who once made one roster move in a full year is now the busiest manager in the building, maybe picking up a bit of that relentless Boston sports-town energy since the move east. From two straight last places to defending champion, Sonny's page is the league's best reminder that it's never too late to start checking the waiver wire.
